obernants.operator: For the real target, exclude a Lagrange polynomial failing its nodal equations, a Bernstein evaluation outside the control convex hull for t in[0,1], and shape-preserving cubic segments with overshoot contrary to their slope construction. Conditional Gauss polynomial exactness excludes wrong integrals only for the stated degree premise in real arithmetic. Native f64 results are not required to satisfy those identities bit-for-bit: their complement contains wrong rounded recurrences, wrong basis/interval coordinates, incorrect knot return values, excess callbacks or inaccurate status bookkeeping. Romberg estimated_error=0 does not exclude a nonzero true integral error; unknown off-sample function behavior remains allowed.

obernants.operator: At fixed distinct nodes and fixed degree<n, a complete set of real nodal ordinates identifies the interpolation polynomial, but one evaluated ordinate leaves an affine coefficient fiber. At Bernstein t=0 only the first control is observed and all later controls remain free; at interior t, perturbations of controls whose Bernstein-weighted sum is zero retain the value. Monotone sample data do not identify the true between-node function. For quadrature samples x_j, f and f+h with h(x_j)=0 have the same sampled execution but may have different integrals; h can be a scaled squared product of (x-x_j). Native rounded equality may enlarge these fibers, and callback budget/status do not restore unsampled information.
